summary: MergeVerifiedEffect._verified_subject never binds the attestation to the invoking run (created_by_run vs request.run_id), unlike the channel-send and promotion paths; the only world check is manifest_hash equality.
failure_scenario: Run A mints a passing merge attestation for subject S under manifest M. Any other run B with the same manifest hash can submit an EffectRequest(run_id=B, attestation_id=A's) for subject S; execute/simulate accept it. I2 says attestations bind the attesting run's sealed world. tests/e2e/test_merge_effect.py's 'forgery matrix' has no cross-run case, so nothing notices.
evidence: Read git.py:_verified_subject (checks action, subject, manifest_hash, ok only); grep shows created_by_run compared in core/effect.py channel/promotion validators but not in effects/git.py. Executed a throwaway probe (deleted afterwards) built on tests/e2e/test_merge_effect.prepared_world: effect.simulate(request.model_copy(update={'run_id': RunId('run-other-same-manifest')})) returned status 'simulated' with no refusal. Pre-existing.

summary: test_every_request_projection_revalidates_its_run_authority (16 cases) and the foreign_run/foreign_manifest cases of test_a_fresh_request_refuses_invalid_authority (line 147) pass without the run-authority guard: JournalDamaged is raised earlier by positive-seal damage, and the assertions use bare pytest.raises(JournalDamaged) with no match.
failure_scenario: The guard validated_channel_send_attestation/validated_attested_channel_request (created_by_run, manifest_hash, subject binding) can be deleted and every projection test still passes, so a regression that accepted a foreign-run or foreign-manifest send proof, once seals are consistent, would not be caught. Each fault edits a sealed row (attestation_json, runs.manifest_hash, channel_messages.attestation_id) without resealing; the seal check fires first.
evidence: Executed: pytest -p <plugin that rebinds _sqlite_channels.validated_channel_send_attestation and validated_attested_channel_request to identity>. Result: 1 failed (fresh[foreign_subject]), 25 passed, including all 16 projection cases and fresh[foreign_run]/[foreign_manifest]. Introduced with this test file.

summary: The wrong_run case of test_current_attempt_writer_requires_its_exact_resume_command never reaches the attempt-writer guard: it is refused earlier at store_command_plan, so the plan.run_id != run_id branch of validated_resume_attempt_command is untested. The shared regex also accepts any of three messages, and the zero-event-count assertion is trivially true for an early refusal.
failure_scenario: Deleting the 'plan targets another run' check in validated_resume_attempt_command leaves the test green. A command whose plan targets another run (from a damaged or migrated plan, not via store_command_plan) could then authorize an attempt event for this run.
evidence: Executed a probe calling _prepare_attempt for each mutation: wrong_run raises 'request and plan target different' from store_command_plan -> seal_current_command_plan -> validated_new_resume_command_plan (never reaching transition_run), while wrong_operation, wrong_fence and wrong_status do reach validated_resume_attempt_command.

summary: test_l0_attempt_law_derives_status_from_the_exact_fence has no lawful RUNNING/RunReclaimed row: every RunReclaimed row is unlawful, so the affirmative path (non-terminal baseline kind -> RUNNING -> RunReclaimed) is untested at the L0 contract.
failure_scenario: A mutation of resume_status_at_fence or validated_resume_attempt_command that refuses every RUNNING reclaim attempt, or that treats unknown baseline kinds as non-resumable, passes this parametrization. The unlawful rows also assert only bare JournalDamaged.
evidence: Read the parametrization (7 rows, RunReclaimed lawful=False in all) against control.resume_status_at_fence, which maps any non-terminal kind to RUNNING. Not mutation-executed.

summary: The cost counter patches only _sqlite_execution_facts._stored_event_from_row_without_relationship; _sqlite_commands.py and _sqlite_capability_provenance.py bind the same function by name via from-import, so projections from those modules are never counted.
failure_scenario: A write path that walks history through the command or capability-provenance projectors (for example resume-attempt baseline validation, or lease/accounting history) can grow with run length while early == late and late <= 4 still hold. The bound is asserted only for one kind of plain append_event.
evidence: grep: _sqlite_commands.py:899/905 and _sqlite_capability_provenance.py:31/311 import and call the function directly; the test uses monkeypatch.setattr on _sqlite_execution_facts only. Source reading; not executed. The open-cost bound (projections < 28*4) is also about 2x looser than the documented ~2x-per-row cost.

summary: The 'strict contract' test only varies floor (and only with a floor-1 valid case); it never asserts floor=0 is accepted, that source='schema8-creation' with floor != 0 is refused, that an unknown source or extra field is refused, or that non-Digest hashes are refused.
failure_scenario: Changing Field(ge=0) to ge=1, dropping _creation_starts_at_zero, or widening source passes this module, although the handoff makes floor-zero creation eras and exact source vocabulary the contract. The handoff test plan promises 'unknown source and noncanonical storage' rejection.
evidence: Read CapabilityAccountingEra in core/control.py against the 25-line test; the only valid case uses floor=1, source='schema7-migration'. Not mutation-executed.

summary: The module claims 'exactly one install ever, at every seam' but test_crash_seams_install_exactly_once covers only effect.after_prepared_commit and effect.before_receipt_txn; effect.after_receipt_update and effect.after_commit, the post-install seams where an install already exists, are not exercised for the git effect.
failure_scenario: A regression that re-installs, or double-reports, when the process dies after the receipt row is updated or committed but before the completion event is appended would not be caught for merge_verified. The forgery matrix also omits cross-run and replayed-attestation cases.
evidence: grep of fault_probe names in src: effect.after_prepared_commit, before_receipt_txn, after_receipt_update, after_commit. tests/e2e/test_fault_injection.py does not mention merge or git. Not executed.

summary: InProcessChannel.append_request accepts two different requests under one attestation_id; the mailbox treats that as JournalDamaged (selector 'message_id = ? OR attestation_id = ?') and test_wake_batch_refuses_two_requests_claiming_one_send_proof depends on it. The double therefore does not exercise the same contract (I6).
failure_scenario: A contract test run on the in-process double accepts a shared send proof that the durable transport refuses, so a caller relying on the double never sees the one-proof-one-request law. In production the adapter binds the proof to message_id, which limits impact.
evidence: Executed a throwaway probe (deleted afterwards): InProcessChannel.append_request(_intent(port='a'),'att-shared') then (_intent(port='b'),'att-shared') both succeed with distinct message ids. Pre-existing.

summary: MailboxChannel.profile hard-codes durability='sqlite_wal' while the journal opens with an unchecked 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' (_sqlite_schema.py:348); SQLite returns the mode it actually selected (delete/memory) on filesystems or paths that cannot do WAL and does not raise.
failure_scenario: On a store where WAL is silently not granted, the published ChannelProfile still claims WAL durability. I4 requires guarantees at real strength.
evidence: Read _sqlite_schema._migrate: the pragma result is discarded and profile is a constant. Not reproduced on a non-WAL filesystem.

summary: ADR 0016 still says the schema-7 migration is 'pending' and 'schema 7 is not yet released', but SCHEMA_VERSION is 9 and v7->v8 and v8->v9 steps exist; the ADR enumerates v7 owners without the later eras it now sits beneath.
failure_scenario: A reader or reviewer uses the ADR to decide whether the 6->7 step may still be amended in place ('complete the existing 6->7 step rather than create a second migration'); with later schemas stacked on top, that licence is stale and could justify rewriting a step that v8/v9 migrations depend on.
evidence: _sqlite_schema.py:112 SCHEMA_VERSION = 9; tests/migrations has test_sqlite_v7_to_v8.py and test_sqlite_v8_to_v9.py; no git tags found. Whether v7 shipped to users is unverified.

summary: The provenance recorder maps sources to producers with owner[id(source)] built by iterating upstream names, so a source object that appears in two upstream outputs is attributed to the last-iterated producer; classification (direct vs transitive) can depend on iteration order. The withdrawn first-pass instrument is documented as failing on the same id() hazard.
failure_scenario: A pass-through output re-exposing an upstream source from a directly connected node could be tallied 'direct' when the source is really transitive, biasing the 'every gather is direct' conclusion. The M7.1 doc already lists incomplete provenance for selectors but not this overwrite.
evidence: Read the instrumentation (owner dict assigned per source in a loop over upstream.get(node.id)). Not executed; the committed 16 rows show no such case, and the doc says the conclusion rests on counterexamples.

summary: scripts/check_capability_provenance_mutations.py: executed in full. All 21 mutants KILLED by assertion failure with passing baselines; every old-text anchor matches exactly once and every pytest node id (including parametrization ids) collects.

Only test_a_page_of_many_waiting_requests (asserts {}) and test_duplicate_requests_are_asked_about_once (asserts {}, 5000 dups < default bind limit) are vacuous but low-impact.
